stories.headline: Epoch AI: Google Controls ~25% of Global AI Compute, Mostly via Custom TPUs

key_facts.fact: Google holds about one quarter of global cumulative AI compute capacity as of Q4 2025, making it the largest single owner of AI compute
key_facts.excerpt: We estimate Google is the largest single owner of AI compute, holding about one quarter of global cumulative capacity as of Q4 2025.

key_facts.fact: About three quarters of Google's compute comes from its in-house designed TPU chips rather than Nvidia GPUs, unlike other hyperscalers who rely predominantly on Nvidia
key_facts.excerpt: Notably among hyperscalers, Google's compute comes primarily from its own custom TPU chips rather than NVIDIA's GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Five hyperscalers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) collectively hold an estimated 71% of global AI compute as of Q4 2025, up from 63% in Q1 2024
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle collectively hold an estimated 71% of the world's cumulative AI compute as of Q4 2025, measured in H100-equivalents of computing power. This is up from 63% in Q1 2024.

key_facts.fact: Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian says AI chip and model demand and revenue justify Google's massive compute spending
key_facts.excerpt: Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud's CEO, says its AI chips and models can help the data centre business gain ground

key_facts.fact: Many AI labs including OpenAI and Anthropic depend almost entirely on hyperscalers for access to their R&D and inference compute
key_facts.excerpt: Many AI labs (including OpenAI and Anthropic) largely depend on these hyperscalers for access to R&D and inference compute.

stories.headline: Beijing Auto Show 2026 Opens as World's Largest, With Humanoid Robots at Every Booth

key_facts.fact: Auto China 2026 features 1,451 vehicles including 181 world premieres and 71 concept cars across a record-breaking 380,000 square meters of exhibition space at two venues
key_facts.excerpt: The show features 1,451 vehicles, including 181 world premieres and 71 concept cars, sprawling across a record-breaking 380,000 square meters of exhibition space at two venues.

key_facts.fact: Humanoid robots and robot dogs were at seemingly every other booth; XPeng plans mass production of its IRON humanoid robot in late 2026, while many other companies simply bought Unitree robots as booth attractions
key_facts.excerpt: Humanoid robots and robot dogs were everywhere, at seemingly every other booth. XPeng, which actually builds its own humanoid robot called IRON and plans to begin mass production in late 2026. But many other companies simply bought a Unitree robot and brought it to their booth as an attraction.

key_facts.fact: Geely unveiled China's first native robotaxi prototype, a purpose-built driverless model with over 3,000 TOPS of computing power, alongside a concept featuring a humanoid robot standing guard
key_facts.excerpt: Geely also unveiled China's first native robotaxi prototype, a purpose-built driverless model developed as a Waymo-like platform with its Galaxy Light concept equipped with over 3,000 TOPS of computing power.

key_facts.fact: The show is now the largest auto show in the world, with 17 halls each containing more EV models than are available in the entire US market
key_facts.excerpt: In a single hall at the show, there were more EV models on display than there are available ones in the entire United States. There are 17 halls at this show. Seventeen.

key_facts.fact: Even non-auto companies like Dreame (robot vacuum maker) displayed electric sports car concepts, while Huawei's Maextro luxury sedan targets the Rolls-Royce segment
key_facts.excerpt: Dreame, a company known for making robot vacuums and stick vacuums, had a massive booth with a red electric sports car concept. Huawei's Maextro luxury sedan was displayed behind velvet ropes like a museum piece.

stories.headline: Wisconsin Regulators Force Data Centers to Pay Full Energy Costs, Block Cost-Shifting to Residents

key_facts.fact: Wisconsin's Public Service Commission unanimously approved a modified special energy rate requiring data centers to pay 100% of new natural gas plant costs, rejecting We Energies' plan that would have shifted 25% to residential customers
key_facts.excerpt: The commission denied We Energies' plan to divide the cost of two new natural gas plants between data centers and existing customers. We Energies proposed that data center companies pay 75% of the plants' capital costs, while other ratepayers cover the remaining 25%.

key_facts.fact: The decision affects Microsoft's Mount Pleasant campus (~900 MW) and a $15 billion Port Washington project for OpenAI and Oracle that could use up to 3.5 GW at full build-out
key_facts.excerpt: The first two phases of Microsoft's data center campus in Mount Pleasant will need around 900 megawatts. The Port Washington project could use up to 3.5 gigawatts at full build out.

key_facts.fact: We Energies plans to spend $19.3 billion on new electricity generation over five years, aiming to double its energy generating capacity by 2030 to serve data centers
key_facts.excerpt: The company is preparing to spend $19.3 billion on new electricity generation over five years. The decision comes as data centers in Mount Pleasant and Port Washington could double We Energies' energy demand by 2030.

key_facts.fact: Regulators lowered the mandatory rate threshold from 500 MW to 100 MW and extended service agreements from 10 to 15 years to prevent cost-shifting during construction phases
key_facts.excerpt: The commission also required projects enroll in the special rate if they use at least 100 megawatts of power. The commission also lengthened data center service agreements from a proposed 10 to 15 years.

key_facts.fact: Nearly 70% of Wisconsin voters said data center costs outweigh their benefits; more than 2,000 public comments were submitted opposing the original plan
key_facts.excerpt: PSC officials said more than 2,000 public comments were submitted.

key_facts.fact: We Energies said the new rate structure could serve as a model for other states looking to meet data center needs while protecting other energy customers
key_facts.excerpt: We Energies has said the new rate could serve as a model for other states looking to meet data center needs while protecting other energy customers.

stories.headline: Samsung Mobile Division Faces First-Ever Annual Loss as AI Devours Memory Supply

key_facts.fact: Samsung MX head TM Roh warned company leadership the mobile division could post its first-ever net loss on smartphones in 2026, despite strong Galaxy S26 sales
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung MX (mobile experience) head TM Roh has warned company leadership that it could be headed for the first net loss on smartphones in the company's history.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia's upcoming Vera AI CPU will use up to 1.5 TB of LPDDR5x memory; a single server rack with 36 Vera CPUs consumes enough RAM for 4,600 Galaxy S26 Ultra devices
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's Vera AI CPU will have up to 1.5 TB of LPDDR5x memory. The CPUs in a single server will consume enough RAM for 4,600 Galaxy S26 Ultra devices (12GB each).

key_facts.fact: RAM now accounts for more than a third of the cost of building a budget phone in mid-2026, roughly doubling the cost of memory and storage according to Counterpoint Research
key_facts.excerpt: According to Counterpoint Research, RAM will account for more than a third of the cost of building a budget phone in mid-2026.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Semiconductor smashed records in Q1 2026, earning an estimated $38 billion (KRW 57.2 trillion) in profit — more than seven times its Q1 2025 net
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Semiconductor has smashed records in the first quarter of 2026, earning an estimated $38 billion (KRW 57.2 trillion) in profit. That's more than seven times its net from Q1 2025.

key_facts.fact: DRAM production in 2027 could fall 40% short of expected demand even with best-case improvements in output, according to Nikkei Asia
key_facts.excerpt: Nikkei Asia projects that won't be enough. Even with best-case improvements in output, DRAM production in 2027 could fall 40 percent short of expected demand.

key_facts.fact: Motorola raised prices on its Moto G budget phones by up to 50%; Samsung added $50-$100 price hikes to Galaxy A37, A57, Z Flip 7, Z Fold 7, and Tab S11
key_facts.excerpt: Motorola recently raised the price of its Moto G budget phones by up to 50 percent. The recently released Galaxy A37 and A57 mid-range devices come with a $50 price hike over the last generation.

stories.headline: ASML Targets 60 EUV Machines in 2026, Pledges No Bottleneck for AI Chip Boom

key_facts.fact: ASML CFO Roger Dassen said the company targets shipping 60 units from its current-gen EUV portfolio in 2026, with room to ramp up to 80 units in 2027 — compared to 44 sold in 2025
key_facts.excerpt: CFO Roger Dassen said ASML targets shipping 60 units from its current-gen EUV portfolio in 2026, with room to ramp up to 80 units the following year.

key_facts.fact: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet pledged the company would prevent supply bottlenecks 'by all possible means' at the AGM, with both logic and memory demand continuing to outpace supply
key_facts.excerpt: Chief Executive Christophe Fouquet, speaking at the Dutch company's annual general meeting, said the firm would prevent bottlenecks 'by all possible means.' Fouquet pointed to persistent tightness for both advanced logic chips and memory chips, saying demand would 'continue to outpace supply' for some time.

key_facts.fact: ASML raised its 2026 revenue outlook to €36 billion-€40 billion after Q1 results showed €8.8 billion in sales and €2.8 billion in net income
key_facts.excerpt: ASML lifted its 2026 revenue outlook to 36 billion-40 billion euros last week, following first-quarter results showing 8.8 billion euros in sales and net income of 2.8 billion euros.

key_facts.fact: Memory makers have sold out inventory for the year and expect supply constraints to persist past 2026, with 51% of Q1 EUV orders coming from memory customers (SK Hynix alone grabbing 20 machines for HBM4 production)
key_facts.excerpt: Memory makers have already sold out inventory for the year and are bracing for supply constraints to stick around past 2026, even with new production lines coming online.

key_facts.fact: TSMC is holding off on ASML's $400M high-NA EUV platform, with Kevin Zhang telling Reuters the chipmaker continues to leverage existing EUV technology for smaller and faster chips
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC's Kevin Zhang told Reuters the chipmaker continues to 'leverag[e] existing EUV technology' to deliver smaller and faster chips, holding off for now on the expensive new platform that runs about $400 million per unit.
